To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

attachment is a relational construct, that is, a set of strategies for regulating proximity seeking and maintaining proximity with attachment figures that are shaped by the quality of the child-parent attachment relationship, that these strategies are organized in a hierarchical structure that includes the attachment system (the most proximal system for attachment), and that the attachment system is embedded in a broader social and personality system, and that attachment relevant experiences shape these systems in ways that are both direct and indirect.

the attachment system is a biologically based motivational system that is designed to ensure the safety and well-being of the individual, and that the way in which individuals regulate their attachment system (e.g. how they seek, receive, and respond to support from others) is shaped by their attachment experiences and is associated with important outcomes in close relationships and in other areas of functioning.

1) attachment relevant experiences shape how individuals think, 2) how individuals think shapes how individuals feel, and 3) how individuals feel shapes how they act in close relationships and in other domains of social and personal functioning [6,7] This is not to say that attachment theory is perfect, nor that the research program is without problems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how attachment patterns and orientations shape the development of social and personality processes across the lifespan.
how early attachment experiences and attachment styles influence later social and personality development.
the role of attachment in social and personality development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
attachment theory is a well-established, empirically supported, and influential theory of personality and social development.
attachment is a dynamic field with an impressive past, a rich present, and a bright future.
attachment theory has been and will continue to be a major source of inspiration for developmental, clinical, and social psychology research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
attachment theory has become one of the most important theoretical and empirical frameworks in social and personality psychology.
the field has been very successful.
attachment is a dynamic construct that shapes the development of the individual and the dyad throughout the lifespan.
The main takeaway from our work is that
attachment is not just about close relationships, it is about everything.

, in adulthood, attachment processes are not limited to close relationships but also influence the development of social and personality characteristics that extend to relationships outside the family of origin (e.g. romantic relationships, friendships, work relationships, and even relationships with strangers).
attachment is not only about close relationships but about the self and the world.
